claims.title: The Margiana oasis civilisation (BMAC)
claims.summary: The Bronze Age Bactria–Margiana Archaeological Complex flourished in the southern Karakum oases, its Margiana centre at Gonur Depe — monumental architecture, irrigation farming and fine metalwork later excavated by Viktor Sarianidi.

claims.title: Rise of the Parthian Empire
claims.summary: The nomadic Parni founded the Parthian state, which grew into an empire ruling Iran and Central Asia for nearly five centuries and rivalling Rome, with Nisa among its early royal centres.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Turkmenistan: From the Bronze Age oases of Margiana and Parthian Nisa, through Silk Road Merv and the Turkmen tribes, to Russian conquest, Soviet cotton and a neutral, gas-rich republic.", terralore.co/country/TKM/chronicle#ev-247bce-rise-of-the-parthian-empire, claim TL:TKM:event:247bce:rise-of-the-parthian-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Royal city of Nisa
claims.summary: Old and New Nisa, near modern Ashgabat, served as an early capital and royal residence of the Parthian Empire, with palaces, temples and treasuries that fused Hellenistic and Iranian art.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Turkmenistan: From the Bronze Age oases of Margiana and Parthian Nisa, through Silk Road Merv and the Turkmen tribes, to Russian conquest, Soviet cotton and a neutral, gas-rich republic.", terralore.co/country/TKM/chronicle#ev-200bce-royal-city-of-nisa, claim TL:TKM:event:200bce:royal-city-of-nisa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nisa inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: The Parthian Fortresses of Nisa were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2007 as an exceptional record of the Parthian civilisation at one of its earliest and most important cities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Turkmenistan: From the Bronze Age oases of Margiana and Parthian Nisa, through Silk Road Merv and the Turkmen tribes, to Russian conquest, Soviet cotton and a neutral, gas-rich republic.", terralore.co/country/TKM/chronicle#ev-2007-nisa-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:TKM:event:2007:nisa-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Merv under the Arab caliphate
claims.summary: After the fall of Sasanian Persia, Merv became a key garrison and administrative centre of the Arab caliphate in Khorasan, a base for the spread of Islam and for campaigns further into Central Asia.

sources.label: State Historical and Cultural Park 'Ancient Merv'

claims.title: Merv as Seljuk capital under Sultan Sanjar
claims.summary: The Great Seljuk sultan Sanjar made Merv a capital; the city's population swelled and it became one of the largest and most cultured cities in the world, a hub of Silk Road science and faith.

sources.label: State Historical and Cultural Park 'Ancient Merv'

claims.title: Mausoleum of Sultan Sanjar
claims.summary: Built at the death of Sultan Sanjar, the great domed mausoleum at the centre of Sultan Kala stands as the finest surviving monument of Seljuk Merv.

sources.label: State Historical and Cultural Park 'Ancient Merv'

claims.title: Mongol destruction of Merv
claims.summary: A Mongol army under Tolui, son of Genghis Khan, besieged Merv during the conquest of the Khwarazmian Empire and massacred its population, ending the city's age as a great metropolis of the Islamic world.

sources.label: State Historical and Cultural Park 'Ancient Merv'

claims.title: Magtymguly Pyragy and Turkmen poetry
claims.summary: The poet Magtymguly Pyragy (1724–c. 1807) wrote in the Turkmen language and called for the unity of the tribes; he is revered as the father of Turkmen literature and national identity.

claims.title: Russians found Krasnovodsk
claims.summary: A Russian military force landed on the eastern Caspian coast and founded the port of Krasnovodsk (now Türkmenbaşy), opening the conquest of the Transcaspian region.

claims.title: Battle of Geok Tepe
claims.summary: General Mikhail Skobelev stormed the Teke Turkmen fortress of Geok Tepe by detonating a mine under its walls; the assault and ensuing massacre of thousands broke Turkmen resistance and secured Russian control of Transcaspia.

claims.title: Russian annexation completed
claims.summary: Following Geok Tepe, the Transcaspian region was annexed as part of the Russian Empire, completing the conquest of the lands of modern Turkmenistan.

claims.title: Creation of the Turkmen SSR
claims.summary: In the Soviet national delimitation of Central Asia, the Transcaspian and Turkmen lands were combined to form the Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic, with Ashgabat as its capital.

claims.title: Collectivisation and cotton
claims.summary: Forced collectivisation seized herds and land and ended Turkmen pastoral nomadism amid fierce resistance, while Soviet planning imposed cotton monoculture across the republic's irrigated land.

claims.title: Ashgabat earthquake
claims.summary: A devastating earthquake struck Ashgabat, destroying the city and killing tens of thousands of people in one of the deadliest seismic disasters in Soviet history.

claims.title: The Kara-Kum Canal
claims.summary: Construction began on the Kara-Kum Canal, which carried water from the Amu Darya across the desert to irrigate the cotton lands — a vast project that opened new farmland at heavy environmental cost.

claims.title: Independence declared
claims.summary: Turkmenistan declared independence from the Soviet Union, with Saparmurat Niyazov as its first president; the United States recognised the new state in December 1991 and opened relations in 1992.

claims.title: Permanent neutrality recognised by the UN
claims.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 50/80 welcoming Turkmenistan's declared permanent neutrality, the basis of its non-aligned foreign policy and a status unique in being recognised by a UN resolution.

claims.title: Niyazov declared president for life
claims.summary: Parliament declared Saparmurat Niyazov ('Türkmenbaşy') president for life, the apex of a personality cult that included renaming the calendar and making his Ruhnama compulsory reading.

claims.title: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow elected
claims.summary: Following Niyazov's death in December 2006, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow was elected president, beginning fifteen years of rule that retained tight one-party control and the neutral, gas-export policy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Turkmenistan: From the Bronze Age oases of Margiana and Parthian Nisa, through Silk Road Merv and the Turkmen tribes, to Russian conquest, Soviet cotton and a neutral, gas-rich republic.", terralore.co/country/TKM/chronicle#ev-2007-gurbanguly-berdimuhamedow-elected, claim TL:TKM:event:2007:gurbanguly-berdimuhamedow-elected, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Serdar Berdimuhamedow succeeds his father
claims.summary: In an early election, Serdar Berdimuhamedow won the presidency over 70 percent of the vote, succeeding his father in a managed dynastic transfer of power, with the elder Berdimuhamedow remaining head of the People's Council.
